title: Analysis of flow-cytometry microbial biofilm datasets with viSNE and Matlab
protocol: Run cyt in Matlab by selecting the cyt directory as the working directory and typing run_cyt into the Matlab prompt.
Choose add data (plus sign) in the GUI to import data.
Import data from .fcs or .csv format using Cyt.
Change file filter to *.csv for importing from .csv format.
Format the .csv file with columns representing measured parameters and each row representing a different measured particle/cell.
Transform the data using hyperbolic arcsin transformation, with cofactor of 150.
Merge or subsample datasets as needed.
Select samples and measurements for analysis by choosing appropriate Gates and Channels in cyt.
Right-click on selected ones to run viSNE (bh-SNE).
Once the algorithm finishes, new channels named bh-SNE1 and bh-SNE2 appear.
Visualize viSNE maps as scatter plots by selecting bh-SNE1 and bh-SNE2 channels and clicking scatterplot.
Adjust visualization options for better data interpretation.
Categorize visual clusters into subpopulations based on expert knowledge and optical/autofluorescent properties.
Delineate identified subpopulations using the polygonal region selection tool in cyt.
Count the number of particles/cells in each delineated region automatically by cyt.
Export analysis from cyt into Matlab by saving the session in cyt.
Load the saved .mat file session into Matlab prompt for further analysis.
Calculate the similarity between different viSNE maps using maximum mean discrepancy as described in mmd_visne.m.
Ensure compared viSNE maps are of equal number of cells and obtained from the same instrument parameters.
Use overlay_visne.m script to project particles/cells not used during viSNE onto a viSNE map.
